definition: Prolong means to make something last longer.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word prolong. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know prolong should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The trainer iced the pitcher's shoulder between innings to prolong his night on the mound.
Extend is the milder act — you can extend a deadline by one tidy day; prolong keeps the whole thing alive past its natural span.
To drag out a meeting goes further than to prolong it: dragging out adds length nobody wants, long past any purpose the meeting had.

To protract is to stretch something out until the stretching itself wearies everyone — protracted negotiations, a protracted lawsuit. Prolong is neutral about whether the extra time is welcome: you can prolong a life or a holiday gladly. Protract almost always complains.

To sustain something is to keep it going at its current level — a singer sustains a note, a runner sustains a pace. It adds nothing beyond the effort of holding steady. Prolong is different: it makes a thing last longer than it otherwise would, pushing the end further away.

The orchestra credits its longevity to a rule that rehearsals end on time.
Prolong means to make something last longer.
The conservators keep the watercolor room dim and cool, and rotate every sheet into dark storage after ninety days on the wall.
Visitors grumble about the gloom.
None of it makes the pigments one shade brighter; it prolongs their life, stretching perhaps two more centuries of visible color out of paper that sunlight would strip in a generation.
Prolong is the right verb because it means to make something last longer — it acts on time and states, never on physical distance.
You can prolong an applause, a career, or a fading color, but not a hallway; a hallway gets lengthened.
The dimness buys duration, and duration is all it buys.
Prolong works on time only: lives, waits, arguments, charges.
Choose extend for boundaries and deadlines, lengthen for physical things, and protract when the stretching itself has become wearying.
Its mirror in this unit is expedite — one stretches a thing's duration, the other clears its path — and note the tone swing: prolonging a life is a triumph, prolonging a meeting is a sin.

No one at the lab expected the probe to last this long.
Its instruments were built for a four-year tour of the outer planets, and the mission should have ended decades ago.
Instead, a small team keeps finding ways to prolong it: shutting down heaters one by one, trimming the data rate, letting nonessential sensors sleep.
Each sacrifice buys another year or two of faint signals from beyond the last planet's orbit.
The engineers joke that their real job is rationing electricity, but the record speaks for them -- a machine outliving its planned life by forty years and counting.
